title: Setting Up Prisma Client
description: Implement the production-grade Prisma Client singleton pattern in Next.js to prevent connection pool exhaustion during hot reload.

data.text: In a standard Node.js server, creating `const prisma = new PrismaClient()` once at the top of your server file works fine. However, in Next.js during local development, **Fast Refresh (Hot Module Replacement)** re-evaluates modules on every code edit. If you instantiate `new PrismaClient()` directly in a route file, each reload creates a brand new client instance with its own internal connection pool, quickly exhausting your database connection limit!

The canonical solution recommended by the Prisma and Next.js teams is to store the PrismaClient instance on the Node.js global object (`globalThis`) in development mode, while using a standard singleton in production.

data.title: lib/prisma.ts (Standard Implementation)
data.content: Place this singleton in lib/prisma.ts or src/lib/prisma.ts and import it across all route handlers, server actions, and server components.

data.text: In Node.js, `globalThis` persists across module re-evaluations during development. When you save a file in Next.js, module-scoped variables are wiped, but `globalThis.prismaGlobal` remains in memory. The nullish coalescing operator (`??`) reuses the existing instance rather than creating a new connection pool.

data.caption: Singleton Lifecycle across Hot Module Reloads
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Code Edit in Next.js] --> B[Next.js triggers HMR]
    B --> C{Does globalThis.prismaGlobal exist?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Reuse existing PrismaClient]
    C -->|No| E[new PrismaClient() & assign to globalThis]
    D --> F[Database Connection Pool Preserved (No Leaks)]
    E --> F

data.title: Production Behavior
data.text: In production (`NODE_ENV === 'production'`), Next.js creates optimized, immutable bundles without HMR. The conditional check ensures `globalThis.prismaGlobal` is only assigned during development, preventing unintended global pollution in serverless lambda environments.

data.title: app/users/page.tsx (React Server Component)
data.content: Direct database access inside Next.js Server Components without API endpoints or client-side fetch waterfalls.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never create `new PrismaClient()` in local function scopes or individual component files.
Use the `globalThis` singleton pattern in `lib/prisma.ts` to survive Next.js Fast Refresh.
Enable query logging in development to observe generated SQL statements and detect slow queries early.
